ucs.title: [LLM] MuddyWater (Mango Sandstorm / Static Kitten) RMM-as-payload — Atera / ScreenConnect / RemoteUtilities pushed via file-share PDF lure
ucs.description: Iran-nexus MuddyWater (a.k.a. MERCURY, Mango Sandstorm, Seedworm, TA450, Earth Vetala) has, since 2020 and especially through the 2022–2024 campaigns documented by Microsoft and Group-IB, replaced traditional macro-droppers with phishing PDFs that link to a file-hosting service (Onehub, OneDrive, Dropbox, Egnyte) hosting a signed Remote Monitoring & Management installer (Atera Agent, ScreenConnect/ConnectWise Control, RemoteUtilities, SimpleHelp, Syncro). The actor uses the RMM itself as the C2/handler, sidestepping AV detection. This UC catches an RMM installer being executed where the droppe

| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(Processes.process) as cmd_lines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents values(Processes.process_path) as paths
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AteraAgent.exe","setup_AteraAgent.exe","AteraAgentSetup.exe","ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientSetup.exe","rutserv.exe","rfusclient.exe","RemoteUtilities.exe","SimpleHelpCustomer.exe","SimpleService.exe","Syncro.Installer.exe","SyncroService.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe")

ucs.kql:
// MuddyWater RMM-payload-via-fileshare hunt — DeviceFileEvents (drop w/ FileOriginUrl) joined to DeviceProcessEvents (execution)
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RMMInstallers = dynamic([
    "ateraagent.exe","setup_ateraagent.exe","ateraagentsetup.exe",
    "screenconnect.clientsetup.exe","connectwisecontrol.clientsetup.exe",
    "rutserv.exe","rfusclient.exe","remoteutilities.exe",
    "simplehelpcustomer.exe","simpleservice.exe",
    "syncro.installer.exe","syncroservice.exe","splashtopstreamer.exe"]);
let VendorDomains = dynamic([
    "atera.com","getatera.com","screenconnect.com","connectwise.com",
    "remoteutilities.com","simple-help.com","syncromsp.com","splashtop.com"]);
let FileShareHosts = dynamic([
    "onehub.com","dropbox.com","mediafire.com","wetransfer.com",
    "drive.google.com","docs.google.com","onedrive.live.com","1drv.ms",
    "sharepoint.com","mega.nz","sendspace.com","files.fm","gofile.io",
    "filebin.net","egnyte.com","box.com"]);
let SuspiciousDrops = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
    | where isnotempty(FileOriginUrl)
    | extend fn = tolower(FileName)
    | where fn in (RMMInstallers)
        or fn matches regex @"(?i)^(atera|screenconnect|connectwise|simplehelp|syncro|splashtop|remoteutilities).*\.(exe|msi|msix)$"
    | extend OriginHost = tolower(tostring(parse_url(FileOriginUrl)["Host"]))
    | where not(OriginHost has_any (VendorDomains))
    | where OriginHost has_any (FileShareHosts)
    | project DropTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DropFile = tolower(FileName), DropPath = FolderPath, FileOriginUrl, OriginHost;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend pfn = tolower(FileName)
| where pfn in (RMMInstallers)
    or pfn matches regex @"(?i)^(atera|screenconnect|connectwise|simplehelp|syncro|splashtop|remoteutilities).*\.exe$"
| join kind=inner SuspiciousDrops on DeviceId
| where pfn == DropFile
| where Timestamp between (DropTime .. DropTime + 1d)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath,
          ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileOriginUrl, OriginHost, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
// MuddyWater RMM-as-payload — ASIM ImProcessCreate (Sentinel has no URL-origin field, so this falls back to RMM exec from staging dirs / browser+archiver parent)
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let RMMInstallers = dynamic([
    "ateraagent.exe","setup_ateraagent.exe","ateraagentsetup.exe",
    "screenconnect.clientsetup.exe","connectwisecontrol.clientsetup.exe",
    "rutserv.exe","rfusclient.exe","remoteutilities.exe",
    "simplehelpcustomer.exe","syncro.installer.exe","splashtopstreamer.exe"]);
let StageDirs = dynamic([@"\downloads\", @"\temp\", @"\appdata\local\temp\", @"\appdata\roaming\", @"\users\public\"]);
let DeliveryParents = dynamic(["outlook.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","winrar.exe","7zfm.exe","acrord32.exe","acrobat.exe","explorer.exe"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| extend pfn = tolower(TargetProcessName)
| where pfn has_any (RMMInstallers)
    or pfn matches regex @"(?i)\\(atera|screenconnect|connectwise|simplehelp|syncro|splashtop|remoteutilities).*\.exe$"
| extend ppath = tolower(TargetProcessName), parent = tolower(ActingProcessName)
| where (ppath has_any (StageDirs)) or (parent has_any (DeliveryParents))
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName,
          TargetProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ucs.title: [LLM] MuddyWater PowGoop loader — GoogleUpdate.exe side-loading rogue goopdate.dll outside the Google Update install path
ucs.description: PowGoop is MuddyWater's bespoke loader, first attributed to MERCURY by Mandiant in 2022 and re-observed through 2024 in campaigns against Israeli logistics and Middle-East government targets. It abuses the legitimate signed Google Update binary (GoogleUpdate.exe) to side-load a malicious goopdate.dll dropped into a writable directory; the DLL decrypts and reflectively loads a PowerShell stager that fetches further MuddyWater payloads. This UC hunts for goopdate.dll being loaded by — or co-resident with — googleupdate.exe from any path other than the canonical Google Update install location, wh
ucs.splunk:
(| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(Processes.process) as cmd_lines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name="googleupdate.exe"
        AND NOT Processes.process_path IN ("*\\Program Files (x86)\\Google\\Update\\*","*\\Program Files\\Google\\Update\\*")
    by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path)
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(Filesystem.file_path) as drop_paths values(Filesystem.process_name) as droppers
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
        where Filesystem.file_name="goopdate.dll"
            AND NOT Filesystem.file_path IN ("*\\Program Files (x86)\\Google\\Update\\*","*\\Program Files\\Google\\Update\\*")
        by host Filesystem.file_name]
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where first_seen >= relative_time(now(),"-14d@d")
| sort 0 - last_seen
ucs.kql:
// MuddyWater PowGoop side-load hunt — goopdate.dll loaded outside canonical Google\Update install path
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let GoogleUpdatePathL = @"c:\program files (x86)\google\update\";
let GoogleUpdatePathR = @"c:\program files\google\update\";
let DllLoads = DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where FileName =~ "goopdate.dll"
    | extend imgpath = tolower(FolderPath)
    | where not(imgpath startswith GoogleUpdatePathL) and not(imgpath startswith GoogleUpdatePathR)
    | project LoadTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, DllPath = FolderPath,
              DllSha256 = SHA256, DllMd5 = MD5,
              LoaderName = InitiatingProcessFileName,
              LoaderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
              LoaderCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              LoaderUser = InitiatingProcessAccountName;
DllLoads
| where tolower(LoaderName) in ("googleupdate.exe","gupdate.exe","googleupdater.exe","goopdate.exe")
    or tolower(LoaderPath) !startswith GoogleUpdatePathL and tolower(LoaderPath) !startswith GoogleUpdatePathR
| union
    (DeviceFileEvents
     | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
     | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed")
     | where FileName =~ "goopdate.dll"
     | extend dpath = tolower(FolderPath)
     | where not(dpath startswith GoogleUpdatePathL) and not(dpath startswith GoogleUpdatePathR)
     | project LoadTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName,
               DllPath = FolderPath, DllSha256 = SHA256, DllMd5 = MD5,
               LoaderName = InitiatingProcessFileName,
               LoaderPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
               LoaderCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
               LoaderUser = InitiatingProcessAccountName)
| order by LoadTime desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
// MuddyWater PowGoop — DeviceImageLoadEvents isn't in Sentinel; fall back to ImProcessCreate (googleupdate.exe from non-canonical path) plus ImFileEvent (goopdate.dll dropped outside install path)
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let GoogleUpdatePathL = @"c:\program files (x86)\google\update\";
let GoogleUpdatePathR = @"c:\program files\google\update\";
let RogueProc = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | extend ppath = tolower(TargetProcessName)
    | where ppath endswith @"\googleupdate.exe"
    | where not(ppath startswith GoogleUpdatePathL) and not(ppath startswith GoogleUpdatePathR)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventType = "RogueGoogleUpdateExec";
let RogueDll = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where EventType == "FileCreated"
    | where tolower(TargetFileName) == "goopdate.dll"
    | extend dpath = tolower(TargetFilePath)
    | where not(dpath startswith GoogleUpdatePathL) and not(dpath startswith GoogleUpdatePathR)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
              TargetProcessName = TargetFilePath, TargetProcessCommandLine = TargetFileName,
              ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventType = "RogueGoopdateDrop";
union RogueProc, RogueDll
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PowGoop Loader DLL Side-Load (MuddyWater / Mango Sandstorm)
id: 7a4d3e0b-5a01-4b8a-9b1e-4f3a8d2c1e9c
status: experimental
description: Detects loading of goopdate.dll from a path outside the canonical Google Update install directory — the load-time invariant of MuddyWater's PowGoop loader, which side-loads a malicious goopdate.dll into the legitimate signed GoogleUpdate.exe to decrypt a PowerShell stager.
references:
    - https://www.mandiant.com/resources/blog/powgoop-mercury-iran
    - https://www.microsoft.com/security/blog/2022/08/25/mercury-leveraging-log4j-2-vulnerabilities-in-unpatched-systems-to-target-israeli-organizations/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense_evasion
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.t1574.002
    - attack.t1036.005
    - attack.g0069
logsource:
    product: windows
    category: image_load
detection:
    selection:
        ImageLoaded|endswith: '\goopdate.dll'
    filter_path:
        ImageLoaded|contains:
            - '\Program Files (x86)\Google\Update\'
            - '\Program Files\Google\Update\'
    condition: selection and not filter_path
fields:
    - Image
    - ImageLoaded
    - Hashes
    - User
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate Google Update component running from a non-default install root (rare; investigate the signer of goopdate.dll)
level: high
